subject: Clarify output ownership exceptions + feedback license (MSA & Order Form)
messages:
From: Amanda Ross <amanda.ross@sysnova.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Annotated order form + IP questions

Dylan —

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached is our annotated Order Form and a short note from procurement/legal with the main open items. Two points that need explicit language before we can proceed:

1) Output ownership: SysNova needs a clear assignment (or license with exclusive rights) to outputs produced by the service based on our prompts and data. We cannot accept broad exceptions that allow Redwood to re-use or assert ownership over customer outputs.

2) Training / data use: We require that Redwood not use any customer prompts, conversation content, or derived outputs to further train or fine-tune models unless we provide explicit opt-in in writing. Aggregated telemetry for service stability is acceptable if it is anonymized and cannot be reverse-engineered.

We also saw a clause in your MSA about a perpetual "feedback" license. We need that narrowed substantially — if Redwood needs a license to use feedback for product improvements, it should be limited, non-exclusive, and explicitly forbid reuse in model training or resale.

Attached: SysNova_OrderForm_Annotated.pdf (annotated with callouts).

Can we get proposed redline language for MSA sections 4.2 (IP), 7.1 (Data use) and the Order Form? If convenient, we can schedule a short call Thurs/ Fri.

Amanda
General Counsel, SysNova
amanda.ross@sysnova.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Ross <amanda.ross@sysnova.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annotated order form + IP questions

Amanda — thanks for the clear note and the annotated order form. Appreciate the directness.

Short answer: we understand the asks and want to get to language that is acceptable to both sides. High-level Redwood positions we intend to propose back:
- Customer Output: we are generally willing to grant customers ownership (or an exclusive/assignable right) to outputs generated from their prompts and data. Need to carve out a narrow exception for outputs that rely on Redwood proprietary system prompts or third-party licensed content that we cannot assign.
- Training/Data Use: Redwood will not use customer-provided prompts, documents, or model outputs to further train or fine-tune our public models unless the customer opts in. We do, however, rely on aggregated and de-identified telemetry for service quality and safety; we think that can remain permitted if explicitly limited.
- Feedback license: we prefer a limited, perpetual (for the purposes of improving the service) non-exclusive license to use feedback, but we can add a clause that prohibits using Customer Data/Outputs to train base models or to create a competing product.

If that aligns generally, I can ask Legal to send concrete redlines to the MSA + Order Form by end of day tomorrow. Would you prefer track-changes on the MSA doc or an inline redline in the Order Form PDF?

Also happy to take a 30m sync Thursday morning.

—Dylan
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Ross <amanda.ross@sysnova.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood proposed redlines (MSA section references)

Amanda / Dylan —

Following Dylan's note, attached is a redline draft of the MSA (Redwood_MSA_Redlines_v3.docx). Summary of the substantive positions and suggested language below so it's easier to review: 

1) Definition: "Customer Output" — proposed definition: 
- "Customer Output" means content, text, images, or other artifacts generated by the Service in direct response to Customer prompts or Customer Data, excluding Redwood System Prompts as defined below.

2) Output ownership assignment
- Proposed language: Customer is granted all rights, title and interest in and to Customer Output, subject to (a) Redwood's pre-existing rights in the Service and System Prompts; and (b) third-party licensed components that are identified in the Order Form.
- Rationale: gives the customer commercial certainty while protecting Redwood IP that we cannot reassign.

3) Training / Model Use
- Proposed language: Redwood shall not use Customer Data, prompts, or Customer Output to train, fine-tune or update Redwood base models or weights without Customer's prior written consent. 
- Permitted: collection of aggregated, de-identified telemetry and usage metrics for Service stability, bug fixes, and safety purposes, provided such telemetry cannot be reverse-engineered to reconstruct Customer Data or Outputs.

4) Feedback License (narrow scope)
- Proposed: Customer grants Redwood a worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free, perpetual license to use Feedback solely to operate, maintain, and improve the Service (including safety mitigations and platform features). Explicitly exclude use of Feedback to (i) train base models; (ii) create or improve non-Redwood models for commercial resale; or (iii) distribute Customer Output to third parties.

5) Audit / Proofs
- If SysNova needs additional assurance, we can offer a compliance statement and summary of telemetry collection practices; for larger accounts we could discuss a limited on-site audit or SOC attestation addendum.

Next steps: if Amanda / SysNova can confirm whether the System Prompts carveout is acceptable, we'll finalize language and prepare the Order Form redline (tracked).

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_Redlines_v3.docx (contains inline tracked changes).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Ethan Moore <ethan.moore@sysnova.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Amanda Ross <amanda.ross@sysnova.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed redlines (MSA section references)

Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the explicit language. A few items SysNova cannot accept without further narrowing: 

1) System Prompts carveout: we need greater specificity. "System Prompts" as written is too broad and could swallow all model behavior. If Redwood insists on a carveout, please enumerate examples and limit to prompts that are hard-coded/system-level strings (e.g., content-safety or diagnostic prompts) and which are not derived from customer interaction.

2) Feedback license: our position is that any license to use feedback must be time-limited and revocable; perpetual, unconstrained licenses are a blocker for us. We will consider a short-term (e.g., 24 month) license for product improvement only, with an express prohibition on using that feedback to train models or to create a derivative commercial product.

3) Training prohibition: unconditional prohibition is our preference. An "opt-in" model is not acceptable unless we receive a clear contractual opt-in for any training use, with a separate addendum.

4) Escrow / output escrow: to address potential disputes over output ownership, we propose a mechanism where, upon notice of a dispute, Redwood places relevant logs/outputs into an escrow repository (access-controlled) for the duration of dispute resolution. This is an unusual ask, but given the sensitivity of outputs in SysNova's workflows we want a failsafe.

Please let us know whether Redwood can accept: (a) a narrower system prompt carveout; (b) a time-bound feedback license; and (c) a contractual escrow mechanism limited to disputed outputs. If not, we will escalate internally.

Best,
Ethan Moore
Senior Counsel, SysNova
ethan.moore@sysnova.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Ross <amanda.ross@sysnova.com>, Ethan Moore <ethan.moore@sysnova.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed redlines (MSA section references)

Amanda / Ethan —

Thanks for the thoughtful feedback and for flagging the Escrow idea. I've pulled Legal and Product together and here's a compromise proposal we think is operational and addresses your commercial concerns: 

1) System Prompts: Redwood will provide an appendix enumerating the categories of system prompts that are excluded from assignment (e.g., hard-coded safety prompts, provider-owned inference templates). This list will be narrow and expressly limited; any extension will need mutual agreement.

2) Feedback license: we can limit the feedback license to 24 months and make it revocable. Crucially, we will add explicit language that Feedback cannot be used to train base models or be sold/transferred to third parties. This mirrors your ask while preserving our ability to improve service quality.

3) Training / Model Use: Redwood will not use Customer Data, prompts, or Customer Outputs to train or fine-tune Redwood base models or to build third-party models unless SysNova provides a separate written opt-in. Aggregated, de-identified telemetry for safety and platform stability is permitted, with technical controls to minimize re-identification risk; we will provide a short technical appendix describing those controls.

4) Escrow for disputed outputs: operationally, we think a lightweight approach will work: upon good-faith notice of a dispute, Redwood will snapshot the relevant logs and outputs and place them in a secure, read-only repository for the dispute period; access will be provided to an agreed neutral arbiter if requested. We're open to further tailoring the process in the SOW.

Next steps: Laura will incorporate the narrow lists and the 24-month revocable feedback clause into the next MSA redline and push the tracked doc to the Drive folder. I'll send over a revised Order Form redline and a proposed DocuSign ready version once legal confirms the final text.

If this matches your expectations, can we aim to finalize by end of week?

Thanks,
Dylan
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
